public_rationale: The records show paying customers and reported cost problems, but neither settles commercial sustainability across big tech. A product can have many subscribers while losing money, and an early loss does not establish permanent nonviability. The unspecified accounting basis also prevents a supported or contradicted financial score under the required rules.
limitations: The loss evidence is secondary reporting, not disclosed product accounts.
A broader definition including embedded AI could change the assessment.
The financial evidence does not establish the separate claim that these developments caused desperation.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Artificial intelligence, among other promised technologies, has not materialized into viable business units for big tech.

statement.excerpt: So many promises — augmented reality, home robotics, autonomous cars, and even then, artificial intelligence writ large — never quite materialized into viable business units, making big tech that little bit more desperate.

from_speaker: never quite materialized into viable business units
our_interpretation: Assess the AI component identified in the normalized proposition, not every technology in the sentence or the separate assertion about desperation.
The context describes developments since 2015 through publication.
The ordinary reading of viable is a commercially sustainable business. Paying customers alone do not establish sustainability.
The principal companies in context are Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon.
No accounting measure or basis is supplied; I will not substitute revenue, customer counts, or parent-company profits for AI-business viability.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable AI-business economics establish that the relevant businesses had not become commercially sustainable by publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes an operating, commercially sustainable AI business within the relevant big-tech companies by publication.

evidence.excerpt: We have over 1 million paid Copilot users.
evidence.locator: Satya Nadella prepared remarks, developer business discussion
evidence.explanation: GitHub Copilot had a substantial paying customer base. This challenges a reading that no commercial AI products existed, but does not establish profitability or sustainable economics.
The article reports product-level cost problems based on Wall Street Journal reporting. It does not establish losses across all relevant businesses or their status in July 2024.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated AI-business financial disclosures with attributable costs, alongside a defensible definition of the business scope and viability measure.
